criterion.purpose: one pre-registered structural intervention on top of round21: give the unchanged N1 head a pooled spatial view of the frozen backbone F8 map, so the screen position of the F1 gap is linearly reachable from the head input, and read the result out mechanistically

intervention.change: a new fusion layer between the frozen trunk features and the unchanged N1 head

spatial_vector.source: F8 [B,96,28,24] from the frozen backbone; F4 [B,64,56,48] is taken from the same call and shape-locked but not used

projection.init: weight and bias exactly zero (nn.init.zeros_), so the delta is 0 at step 0

intervention.fusion: fused = features + projection(spatial); arm A bypasses the layer and freezes it at zero
intervention.head: TacticalPolicy.forward_features with exactly one line changed: the incoming `features` is not detached (the parent detaches it, which would leave the fusion layer with zero gradient for all 200 updates, making arm S vacuous); a unit test asserts the two forwards are bitwise identical on identical inputs and that the body is the parent body with that one line changed
intervention.base_logits: still backbone.policy_head(original features), never recomputed from the fused vector, so the residual head keeps its round20/21 meaning
intervention.not_changed: worlds, world parameters, R19 split, round21 renderer and pixels, teacher actions, labels, pixel packing, encoder, loss weights, optimizer, learning rate, clip, sequence, batch, update count, seed set, closed-loop runner, condition, masking
intervention.parameter_increment: S adds exactly 24320 active parameters (94*256+256); A adds 0 and keeps round21's 429200

data.source: round21 run/records.json assets, reopened read-only and SHA-bound per event; nothing re-rendered, no teacher called, no new label created

train.use: the only events encoded or trained on

validation.use: read-only: never trained, never labelled, never encoded into the training set; closed loop and input probes only

data.bindings: pixels.npz, history.pt, labels.pt and rollout.json must equal round21's frozen SHA table for all 14 train events, otherwise the run aborts

arms.A: fusion bypassed and frozen at zero: round21 arm A
arms.S: fusion live from a zero initialisation

training.precision: FP32 without AMP, autocast disabled, matmul TF32 False, cuDNN TF32 False, float32 matmul precision highest
training.loop: round20 train_all with two additions only: the fused feature and the saved fusion state
training.initialization: fresh seed reset per construction; the initial head SHA must equal the frozen R16/R20/R21 table for the seed and the two arms must agree bitwise; the fusion layer must start at exactly zero in both arms
training.equivalence: because the fusion starts at exactly zero and arm A is bypassed, step 0 of arm S is bitwise arm A; a unit test asserts identical policy logits and identical masked actions on real data rows
training.control_reproduction: arm A must reproduce round21's A checkpoint and its closed-loop rows bitwise; if it does not, that is reported as `control_not_reproduced` and the S-vs-A comparison is withheld
training.selection: final step only: no early stopping, no validation-based selection, no tuning

evaluation.order: all six checkpoints written and SHA-frozen first; then the six R18 baselines, then B0, then the six checkpoints, validation before train
evaluation.executor: round21.run_event_rendered / round21.closed_loop reused verbatim, so the evaluation code is round21 code and not a copy
evaluation.b0: the frozen baseline policy logits on the identical telegraph renders; a reference, not a capability
evaluation.six_baselines: round20.six_baselines re-executed on the same worlds; the 168 rows must equal round21's
evaluation.holdout_rule: if ANY of the six R18 baselines is feasible on ANY validation event the R18 filter has failed on the holdout side: report it verbatim and withhold the learning conclusion

definitions.direction: rebuild the logical-frame x trace from the executed actions with `advance` semantics (round21.gap_trace), take the canonical displacement start -> wall_frame-1: that is `direction`; `screen_direction` is the same displacement in raw x
definitions.toward: the canonical direction points from the start's canonical x at the gap's canonical centre, so `toward` is "moved toward the slot" regardless of the mirror; `away` is the opposite and `hold` is zero net motion
definitions.parked: `signed_error_px` is measured at wall_frame-1 in canonical px: 0 inside [gap0, gap1], negative short of the left edge, positive past the right edge
definitions.mirror_flip_rate: the fraction of mirror-group cells whose canonical motion is toward the gap; because the same screen-right prior is right in the base group and wrong in the mirror group, this is the direction flip this round is about
definitions.identical_cells: for every seed, the number of the 14 validation events on which the two arms have the same first-hit frame (a stricter "unchanged" than the F1 count alone)

primary_metrics: F1 holdout, per group (base / mirror) and per arm: cells that move toward the gap, hold, or move away, plus the mirror toward rate (the direction flip rate this round is about)
F1 holdout, per cell: whether the decision-time x is inside the gap at wall_frame-1 and the signed parking error in px (negative = short of the left edge, positive = past the right edge)
per family F1/F2/F3 and pooled: feasible and survived per network, every event first hit, totals, and for each seed the number of validation events whose first hit is identical between the arms

discriminating evidence for "base prior" vs "spatial information unavailable": the stored prediction distribution per mirror group, an input-mirror flip probe on every head, a linear decodability probe of the 94-d vector and of the 256-d trunk features, the frozen B0 bias, a decomposition of the learned delta into a constant re-bias and a screen-dependent part, and a within-checkpoint delta-on/delta-off ablation that changes no parameter

probe_caveats.flip: the probe mirrors the whole playfield, so the player sprite is mirrored too; a flipped preference therefore cannot be attributed to the gap alone. It is reported with its moving-step denominator, and the distilled heads hold on almost every telegraph-window decision, so its power is small by construction
probe_caveats.decodability: the probe fits on F1 train pixels only and leaves one geometry group out; its conclusion is reported together with a seven-order lambda sweep so that it does not rest on one shrinkage value, and p >> n means a small lambda is an interpolator
probe_caveats.ablation: the S head was trained with the delta, so "delta off" is a counterfactual, not arm A

evaluation.reporting: per family, never only aggregated; n=3 seeds; F2 validation has one group; mirrors are not independent samples; every F1 cell is listed
evaluation.degeneracy: single_candidate and switches<=1 are counted, listed and reported, never dropped

verdict_rules.equivalence: arm A must reproduce round21's A checkpoint SHA and every closed-loop row bitwise; if it does not, the round reports `control_not_reproduced` and withholds the S-vs-A conclusion
verdict_rules.improvement: F1 validation feasible per seed, S minus A: any seed strictly greater = improved, all equal = unchanged, any seed lower = worse
verdict_rules.mechanism: the mirror toward rate and the parking errors are reported as counts and px, never as a significance claim; a failure to move them is reported as a failure
verdict_rules.honesty: if the mirror direction does not improve, the round must state which of the two readings the evidence supports (base prior vs vector too coarse) instead of leaving it open

claims.significance: none: 3 seeds, 7 validation groups, at most 14 independent geometries; descriptive only
claims.gate: no formal gate opened, no deployable checkpoint produced, no game executed
claims.can_show: whether a 94-d pooled spatial view of the same frozen backbone is enough for the same N1 head to stop being dominated by the screen-right prior, and if not, whether the reason is the prior or the vector
claims.cannot_show: tactical understanding, learnability beyond these 7 held-out geometries, or that any policy reads a telegraph the way a player would

criterion.failure_policy: first failure retained; one run; no retrain, rerun, repair of numbers, extra epoch, tuning or baseline switch

split.rule: one group = base + mirror, atomic; within each family the groups are ordered by group name (candidate index) and alternate train/validation starting with train at index 0; the two F2 groups therefore give one train and one validation group

fusion.init: weight and bias exactly zero (nn.init.zeros_), so the delta is 0 at step 0
fusion.definition: F8 -> 7x6 average pool over channels (42) + channel-and-row mean per column (24) + channel-and-column mean per row (28) = 94, then Linear(94,256) initialised at exactly zero; arm A bypasses the layer and keeps it frozen at zero
fusion.private_calls: backbone._checked_regions, backbone._playfield_input and backbone.playfield are called in the same order forward_core calls them; a unit test recomputes forward_core's tail from the extracted F4/F8 and asserts bitwise equality

resolution.note: the F8 column axis is the screen-x axis: 192 model columns / 24 = 8 model px per column, i.e. 16 native playfield px, so a 12-20 px gap is about one F8 column wide and the frozen vector is coarse by construction

initialization.method: fresh seed reset immediately before every N1 construction after the backbone load, through the frozen r16 recipe; the fusion layer is built afterwards and zero-initialised, so it cannot move the head initialisation

round21_reference.f1_deaths: round21: every F1 death (validation 24 + train 27 + B0 12) is on wall_frame

prerequisites: every training asset equals round21's frozen SHA
the spatial vectors recompute to the frozen digest
the initial head SHA equals the frozen table for every seed
the six R18 baselines reproduce round21's 168 rows
verification.control: arm A must equal round21's A checkpoint SHA and its closed-loop rows for all 3 seeds; otherwise it is reported as `control_not_reproduced` and the S-vs-A comparison is withheld
verification.step0: a unit test asserts that step 0 of arm S is bitwise arm A (identical policy logits, identical masked action, delta exactly 0)

failure_policy: first failure retained; one run; no retrain, rerun, repair, overwrite, extra epoch or baseline switch
